answer: An agent economy curbs Sybil attacks by anchoring node identities to low-power whisper beacons regulated by quartz crystal clocks. Field stations at a desert oasis verify physical presence by cross-measuring radio time-of-flight between nodes. An attacker incurs substantial capital and site-deployment costs for each physical transceiver rather than spinning up virtual agents. However, intense thermal shimmering distorts radio propagation delays, occasionally rejecting honest participants.
